verdict_reason: _compute_landscape reproduces Bubenik 2015's definition lambda_k(t) = k-max_i max(0, min(t-b_i, d_i-t)) with a maximum absolute difference of EXACTLY 0.0 on a 12-bar diagram sampled at 100 grid points over [births.min(), deaths.max()], for k = 1..3. It is also correctly scale EQUIVARIANT -- landscapes carry units -- with lambda(s*D) = s*lambda(D) to rel 1e-9 at s = 1e-6, 1e-3, 1e3, 1e6.
comparable_reason: GUDHI's representations.Landscape uses the ROTATED-frame convention and is exactly sqrt(2) times this one: measured ratio 1.414214 on every nonzero sample, max|gudhi - sqrt2*bubenik| = 1.67e-16. Neither is wrong, but a BLME landscape value and a GUDHI-derived value are not directly comparable. Both conventions are now pinned in the parity test. Separately, 30 emitted keys carry 'meta' MID-NAME (layer_0_h0_meta_prescale = 1.0, layer_0_h0_meta_last_entry_is_block_output, ...); the repo convention is the _meta_ PREFIX, so all 30 count as public features. A sweep of all 51 tasks found this in exactly one task.
github_reason: Executed gudhi.representations.Landscape on the same diagram and sample range. It agrees with the tent definition up to the sqrt(2) rotated-frame convention; BLME agrees with the definition exactly.
paper_reason: Bubenik 2015 defines the landscape but publishes no number tied to this corpus protocol.
confounds_reason: 30 metadata keys enter the feature table because 'meta' is embedded mid-name rather than used as the _meta_ prefix; several are constants (prescale = 1.0) and at least one is a provenance boolean.
